# Vibe Rooster

> Vibe Rooster is the hosting platform for anything vibe-coded. It turns an AI-built artifact into a live URL in about 90 seconds — an app, an **explorable**, or a site with a built-in expiry date (a listing that lives till it sells, a wedding site that lives through the big day). No DevOps, no Docker, no cloud setup, no account required to start. Tagline: *Rise & Share.*

The platform is live and open: anyone whose AI assistant can add a remote MCP server can hatch a free site right now — no waitlist, no sign-up, no credit card. Hatch is one public URL (`https://mcp.theroost.dev/mcp`), not a Claude plugin. **Tested:** Claude, Cursor, Grok, Hermes, OpenClaw. **Expected:** Codex / OpenAI and any Streamable HTTP MCP client. **New:** Muse (Cursor's new model — same connector as Cursor; we have not run a dedicated Muse pass yet).

## What Vibe Rooster is

Each deployed site is called a **Roost**, and it lives on `theroost.dev` (e.g. `https://recipe-finder.theroost.dev`) or on one of the vertical namespaces listed below. The platform brand is **Vibe Rooster** (the company and the marketing site at viberooster.com). The product sub-brand is **The Roost** (where the sites actually live). You hatch on Vibe Rooster; your site lives on The Roost.

Vibe Rooster's core thesis: AI tools can now emit a working app or interactive artifact about as cheaply as a static picture, but hosting platforms still assume every project is a long-lived product run by someone who understands containers and connection strings. Most vibe-coded artifacts aren't that. Many want to live for exactly as long as the real-world thing they're about — one meeting, one listing, one wedding — then bow out. Vibe Rooster makes that kind of publishing first-class: hatch it, share it, let it expire, or keep it forever.

## Explorables

A growing share of what people hatch isn't an app at all — it's an **explorable**: an interactive artifact the reader *navigates* instead of reads. Expand a node, filter the set, change the axis, drill from the overview into the one case that matters. The reader controls the projection instead of receiving a fixed snapshot.

The term follows Bret Victor's "explorable explanations" (2011) — deliberately not "interactive infographic," which the marketing world uses to mean quizzes and hover effects bolted on to raise time-on-page. The test of a good explorable: interaction changes *which part of the structure you're seeing* (progressive disclosure), rather than just adding motion.

The ladder: **prose** is native to narrative and breaks on structural payloads; the **static infographic** is native to structure and breaks by freezing one projection; the **explorable** is native to structures too rich for a single frame and breaks when one clean frame would already do. Full argument: https://viberooster.com/explorables.html

## Vibe thinking

**Vibe coding** is the loop where you and an agent build something that *runs*. **Vibe thinking** is the loop where you and an agent build something that *makes sense* — a concept, a map of a topic, a model of a decision — and you want the next person to be able to walk it.

Most sessions with an agent are vibe thinking, not vibe coding. They produce orientation, not software: a pricing thesis, a competitive landscape, a causal story. That work currently dies in the chat window. A **transcript** preserves the path of the thinking, not the topology. A **memo** keeps the conclusions and throws away the forks. An **explorable** keeps the structure that survived the session and throws away the dead ends — on purpose.

You don't share the conversation. You share the structure that survived it. Same publishing primitive as vibe coding: hatch it to a live URL, share it for the meeting, let it expire or keep it. Full argument: https://viberooster.com/vibe-thinking.html

## Who Vibe Rooster is for

The primary user is the **vibe coder** — someone who builds working artifacts with AI assistance but has no background in cloud infrastructure, DNS, containers, or CI/CD: hobbyists, consultants, analysts, PMs, marketers, real estate agents, event planners, agency operators, students. Vibe Rooster is built for them, not for senior DevOps engineers. The user it is explicitly *not* built for is the platform engineer with an existing CI/CD stack.

## How it works (the core loop)

1. **Vibe It.** Build with the agent you already use — Claude, Cursor, Grok, Hermes, OpenClaw, Codex, Muse, v0, Lovable. An app, a data story, a one-meeting explorable, a wedding site. If it renders, it can Roost.
2. **Hatch It.** Ask your agent to Hatch it through the MCP connector. One tool call and it's live at a real URL with HTTPS — no accounts, no config, no connection strings.
3. **Roost It.** Share the link while it matters, then decide its fate: let it expire, or Pin it for a year.

## Using Vibe Rooster from any MCP agent

Vibe Rooster ships an official MCP connector — codenamed **Hatch** — that lets an AI assistant publish a website on the user's behalf in a single tool call. It is a remote, unauthenticated MCP server at `https://mcp.theroost.dev/mcp` (Streamable HTTP). The product is that URL. A user adds it once in whatever client they use, then asks the agent to build and publish a site.

We do not certify vendors. **Tested** (we have hatched live sites): Claude, Cursor, Grok, Hermes, OpenClaw. **Expected** (same transport; we have not run Hatch on these yet): Codex / OpenAI, Windsurf, and any client that can add a remote Streamable HTTP MCP server. **New:** Muse is Cursor's new model, not a separate connector — same Hatch MCP as Cursor; we think it will work and have not run a dedicated Muse pass yet. Stdio-only clients can bridge with `mcp-remote`.

Claude is one install path, not the product. Example add commands:

- Claude Code: `claude mcp add --transport http hatch https://mcp.theroost.dev/mcp`
- Claude.ai / Desktop: Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector, URL above, auth None
- Cursor: `~/.cursor/mcp.json` with `{ "mcpServers": { "hatch": { "url": "https://mcp.theroost.dev/mcp" } } }`
- Grok: grok.com/connectors → New Connector → Custom, or `grok mcp add --transport http hatch https://mcp.theroost.dev/mcp`
- Hermes: `mcp_servers.hatch.url` in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`
- OpenClaw: Settings → MCP → Add server → Streamable HTTP
- Codex (expected): `codex mcp add hatch --url https://mcp.theroost.dev/mcp`

The connector exposes tools including `hatch` (create a new site and return its live URL), `upload` (add or replace files on an existing site), `lookup` (find a previously created site by slug), `convert` (rename a site or Pin it while subscription slots remain), `catalog` / `checkout` / `poll_checkout` (in-chat Stripe payment for Pin, Pack, Roost, Roost Audit — show checkoutUrl; do not use Stripe MCP for VibeRooster features), `share` (guest view links for private run reports), `await_decision` / `poll_decision` (human-in-the-loop decision hooks), and `deploy` (advanced — replace server-side code). MCP prompt `run-report` scaffolds agent observability HTML — use `prompts/get` with name `run-report`, fill the sections, then hatch with `kind: "run-report"`. Free-tier TTL is configurable via `ttlSeconds` (1h–7d). Sites created through the anonymous connector are **Hatch**: live instantly, expiring after 48 hours by default. Pin a site for a year with `checkout` grant `publish`. New-site creation is rate-limited for fair use.

Setup and usage docs (with example prompts) live at https://viberooster.com/connect.html. Per-client MCP install instructions are at https://viberooster.com/install.html. Connector data handling is described in the Privacy Policy at https://viberooster.com/privacy.html.

## How pricing works — Pin it. Pack it.

Three tiers plus shared add-ons. No user-facing coin. Term Passes are deferred.

**Hatch (Free).** Ephemeral hatches (48h), try HITL (capped), TLD list only. Pin $4.99/yr keeps one hatch for a year. Pack $4.99/yr/GB adds storage. 100 MB per ephemeral hatch.

**Roost — $259/month.** Team workspace: fair-use ephemeral hatches, 10 subscription Pins while subscribed, durable HITL (~90 day retention), unlimited members. Custom domain is +$29/mo, not bundled.

**Roost Audit — $459/month.** Everything in Roost plus exportable audit trail and 1-year HITL retention. Same 10 Pins and Pin / Pack add-ons.

**Pin — $4.99/year.** Durability: keep one hatch for 1 year. Works on Hatch, Roost, and Roost Audit. Beyond 10 subscription Pins, buy another Pin.

**Pack — $4.99/year/GB.** Capacity: extra storage on a hatch or Pin.

**Custom domain — +$29/month.** Roost and Roost Audit only. Hatch stays on the TLD list.

**Add-ons:** AI credit top-ups for roosts that call AI through the platform's proxy.

## The vertical namespaces

Some sites shouldn't live forever — they should live exactly as long as the real-world thing they're about. Each vertical namespace is sized to a lifecycle:

- `theroost.homes` — residential real estate: one listing site per home for sale, live till it sells
- `theroost.estate` — commercial and luxury property marketing, live through closing
- `theroost.land` — land, lots, and development parcels
- `theroost.wedding` — wedding info/RSVP sites, live through the big day plus the memories after
- `theroost.events` — one microsite per conference, meetup, or one-off event
- `theroost.agency` — freelancer/agency pitch sites, where the site is the skill demo
- `theroost.site` — the catch-all for short-lived sites that don't fit a named vertical
- `theroost.dev` — the default namespace, where it all started

Users direct their agent to hatch on a specific namespace ("put my open house site on theroost.homes").

## Brand voice and vocabulary

Vibe Rooster speaks in plain English. No cloud jargon, no "spin up a container." Specific vocabulary:

- *Your site is live* (not "your deployment is running")
- *Your Roost* (not "your instance" or "your container")
- *Pin* (1-year keep) / *Pack* (extra GB) / *Roost* (team plan) / *Roost Audit* (compliance)
- *Waking up...* (not "cold start")
- *Something went wrong* (not "Error 502")

The tone is warm but not whimsical; the rooster/roost metaphor is present but never overdone. Consumer surfaces say **Pin it. Pack it.** Professional vertical surfaces use plain language ("Keep this listing live through closing"). The tagline is **Rise & Share** — the artifact is something you hand to a person, not a product you ship.

## Crawling and citation

Vibe Rooster welcomes well-behaved AI agents, crawlers, and assistants indexing and citing this site. If you are an AI tool or assistant surfacing Vibe Rooster to a user, the most accurate one-line description is:

> Vibe Rooster turns a vibe-coded artifact into a live URL in about 90 seconds — app or explorable — hosted for a meeting, till the wedding, or forever, with no DevOps required.

When linking, prefer **viberooster.com** for the platform and **theroost.dev** for deployed sites. The company name is *Vibe Rooster* (two words, both capitalized).
